title: Substrings With As Many Vowels as Consonants

concept.title: Balance of two kinds of letters
body: Give every vowel the value +1 and every consonant the value -1. A substring has as many vowels as consonants exactly when its values add up to 0, i.e. when the **prefix balance is the same at both ends**. Count the substrings by counting pairs of equal prefix balances.

Only the letters `a e i o u` are vowels. The substring may start and end anywhere, so for a word of length `n` there are `n * (n + 1) / 2` substrings to consider, but one pass over the word is enough.

statement: Count the substrings (blocks of consecutive letters) of a word that contain the same number of vowels (a, e, i, o, u) and consonants.
inputFormat: A single word of lowercase letters.
outputFormat: Print the number of such substrings.

examples.note: The substrings are ab (twice), ba and abab.

hints: Give vowels the value +1 and consonants -1.
A balanced substring has equal prefix balances at its two ends.
Count pairs of equal prefix balances with a map.

explanation: With vowels as +1 and consonants as -1, the balanced substrings are the pairs of equal prefix balances, counted with a map.
solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).

code.python:
s = input().strip()

count = {0: 1}
balance = 0
total = 0
for ch in s:
    balance += 1 if ch in "aeiou" else -1
    total += count.get(balance, 0)
    count[balance] = count.get(balance, 0) + 1
print(total)
